operations.summary: atomically increments both balance_dollars and balance_cents for one wallet
backfills balance_cents from balance_dollars via SELECT then per-row UPDATEs in separate transactions

conflicts.risk_explanation: credit does atomic balance_cents = balance_cents + amount while resync does read balance_dollars then blind-write balance_cents = dollars*100 in a later transaction. If resync SELECT precedes credit and UPDATE follows it, the credit increment to balance_cents is lost and NULL+amount stays NULL.

resync reads balance_dollars to derive cents while credit concurrently increments balance_dollars. Stale read of balance_dollars causes stale derived cents to overwrite the already-incremented balance_cents, leaving dollars correct but cents inconsistent.

tests.name: credit_vs_resync_stale_overwrite
tests.rationale: Synced wallet plus concurrent increment and backfill. Resync reads stale balance_dollars before credit and blind-writes stale cents after, losing the credit's balance_cents increment while balance_dollars stays correct.

invariants.description: cents includes 500c credit and stays in step

tests.name: credit_on_null_vs_resync_backfill_race
tests.rationale: Pre-backfill wallet with balance_cents NULL. credit does balance_cents+amount which stays NULL in Postgres; resync must fill it. Stale SELECT before credit causes resync to write 1000 instead of 1500, and any serial order yields 15/1500.

invariants.description: dollars includes credit from NULL start

tests.name: two_credits_vs_resync
tests.rationale: Two distinguishable credits widen the race window. Serially final is always 30/3000; concurrent stale resync can lose one or both cent increments while dollars still sums correctly.

tests.name: multiroom_resync_snapshot_vs_credits
tests.rationale: Resync SELECTs both wallets at once then UPDATEs each in its own transaction. Credits on different wallets interleaved between snapshot and per-row writes cause stale cents overwrite on one or both wallets.
